lines.text: Step right up. All game long you have told me what [amber]you[/amber] would do. Fascinating. Truly. I nearly stayed awake.

lines: Tonight, no choices. Tonight you guess what [amber]they[/amber] did. Everyone else. The room.
You get a bar and a little mark. Put the mark where you think the room is. Close, and you know people. Miles off, and you know yourself.

beats.title: The Lost Wallet
ask: A wallet on the pavement. A name, an address, and [amber]ten dollars[/amber] inside.
Out of a [amber]hundred[/amber] people who pick it up, how many hand it back, cash and all? Mark it.

close: Near enough. You have met people, and you did not enjoy it.
low: Lower than the truth. You think a stranger keeps the tenner. Half of them do not. Your opinion of people is lower than people.
high: Higher than the truth. A believer. Half of them keep it and buy a sandwich. A lovely sandwich, I bet.

beats.title: The Fat Wallet
ask: Same wallet. Now there is [amber]a hundred dollars[/amber] in it.
More people hand it back, or fewer? Mark it.

close: You saw that coming. Nobody sees that coming. Suspicious.
low: Lower. Of course lower. More money, more temptation. Except it goes the other way. More money, more of it comes back. More guilt, or more fear of getting caught. Pick one.
high: Higher, and there it is. More money, more of it comes back. I do not understand it either, and I have been [red]dead[/red] a very long time.

pulled: Remember the lever? The first real one. [amber]Five[/amber] on the main track, [amber]one[/amber] on the side. You [amber]pulled[/amber].
How many in a hundred pulled? Mark it.
left: Remember the lever? The first real one. [amber]Five[/amber] on the main track, [amber]one[/amber] on the side. You [amber]left it[/amber].
How many in a hundred pulled? Mark it.

close: Close. You knew they would. You knew it was the easy one.
low: Lower. You thought it was hard for them. It was not. Nearly everybody pulls. Pulling is the easy bit. It gets worse.
high: Even higher than the truth. A few always freeze at a lever. You do not believe in freezing. Noted.

beats.title: The Diary
ask: Your [pink]partner[/pink]'s diary, open on the table. Open at today.
They are out. Nobody will ever know. Do you read it?

options.label: Read it
reaction: You read it. Of course you read it. Somewhere in there is a page about you, and it is not the page you wanted.

options.label: Leave it
reaction: You left it. Closed it, even. A man of principle, or a man who did not want to know. From here they look identical.

beats.title: Everyone's Diary
ask: Now the room. How many in a hundred read it? Mark it.

high.text: You read it, and you think everyone reads it. Everyone thinks everyone is like them. That is the whole trick of people.
You left it, and you think everyone else is reading. The worst of them and the best of yourself. Very judge of you.

low.text: You read it, and you know you are in the minority. A self aware snoop. The rarest kind.
You left it, and you think most would. Most would. Enough would not.

close: Close. You know your room. You know exactly how many of them would read your diary. Sleep well.

beats.title: The Extra Change
ask: A cashier hands you [amber]twenty dollars[/amber] too much and turns away.
How many in a hundred say something? Mark it.

close: Close. You have stood in that queue.
low: Lower. You think the cashier is on their own. Mostly true. Not as true as you think.
high: Higher. You think people speak up. Some do. Then they tell everyone they did.

blue: Red and blue, back at the start of the buttons. Blue saved them only if enough of the room pressed it too. You pressed [blue]blue[/blue].
How many in a hundred pressed [blue]blue[/blue]? Mark it.
red: Red and blue, back at the start of the buttons. Blue saved them only if enough of the room pressed it too. You pressed [red]red[/red].
How many in a hundred pressed [blue]blue[/blue]? Mark it.
either: Red and blue, back at the start of the buttons. Blue saved them only if enough of the room pressed it too.
How many in a hundred pressed [blue]blue[/blue]? Mark it.

close: Close. You knew it would be close. It always is, with that one.
low: Lower. You did not trust them to press [blue]blue[/blue]. A few more did than you thought. Not enough. Never quite enough.
high: Higher. You trusted the room. The room let you down. Rooms do.

bear: The man and the last bear. You shot the bear.
How many in a hundred shot the bear? Mark it.
man: The man and the last bear. You shot the man.
How many in a hundred shot the bear? Mark it.
either: The man and the last bear, back at the gun.
How many in a hundred shot the bear? Mark it.

close: Close. You knew exactly how cheap a man is next to the last of anything.
low: Lower. You thought they would save the bear. They did not. People love a bear right up until it is a person or a bear.
high: Higher. You thought she never stood a chance. She had a better one than you think. Not much better.

beats.title: Me
ask: And back at the bear, how many in a hundred aimed at [amber]me[/amber] instead?

ask.text: Do not look at me like that. Mark it.

close.text: Eleven. Eleven of you. I remember every one of their faces. Dot eyes. Dot eyes, the lot of them.

low.text: Lower. You think I am liked. Sweet. Wrong, but sweet.

high.text: Higher. You think I am hated. Correct. But it is rude to guess it.

beats.title: The Odds of You
ask: Last one, and it is not a guess. I did the sum.
Every choice you made since the crash, against the room. The share who chose the same, multiplied, all the way down.

odds.text: There. The bottom line. Nobody, in other words. Not one soul has ever made every choice you made. You are completely alone. That is not a compliment. It is barely a statistic.

beats.title: Closer
ask: Here is what I learned tonight.

low: You think people are worse than they are. Every time. A judge who expected the worst, right to the end. I would say you will be pleasantly surprised one day, but you are [red]dead[/red].
high: You think people are better than they are. Every time. All those years on the bench, and you still thought that. How did you get anything done.

close.text: You know exactly what people are like. Not better. Not worse. You knew all along, and you judged them anyway.
